# Adjudication Task — Chapter 847

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃847화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|천하는 광활하다.
  6|
  7|그러나 천하(天下)라는 두 글자에 담긴 의미 그대로, 그 모든 것의 위에는 하늘이 있었다.
  8|
  9|드넓은 대지와 바다. 살아 있는 것과 죽은 것.
 10|
 11|그 무엇 하나 하늘을 피해 숨을 수 없다.
 12|
 13|구름과 함께 아득한 창공을 가로지르는 날짐승조차, 끊임없이 번영과 몰락을 거듭하며 서로를 향해 날붙이를 겨누는 인간들조차 하늘을 우러러본다.
 14|
 15|과연 저 위에는 어떤 대단한 존재가 있을까 하는 의문과 함께.
 16|
 17|사람들에게 있어 하늘이란 바로 그런 것이었다.
 18|
 19|그저 바라보기만 할 뿐, 결코 닿을 수 없는 미지의 영역. 두려워하면서도 공경해 마지않는 대상.
 20|
 21|그렇기에 천하를 손에 넣은 이가 천자(天子)라 불리게 된 것은, 어쩌면 너무나도 당연한 일이었을 것이다.
 22|
 23|세상 모든 것을 내려다보는 저 푸른 하늘이야말로 절대적인 권위의 상징이었으니까.
 24|
 25|‘하지만 그런 천자도 결국 한낱 인간이지. 다른 이의 애첩까지 빼앗는 걸 보면.’
 26|
 27|조금 전의 놀라움은 순식간에 사라지고 실소가 빈자리를 채운다.
 28|
 29|피식 웃는 적천강의 모습에 호위장이 떨떠름한 표정을 지었다.
 30|
 31|“그리 웃긴 이야기는 아니었습니다만.”
 32|
 33|“아니, 듣는 입장에서는 충분히 우스웠다. 결국 천자라고까지 불리는 자가 신하의 애첩을 빼앗고, 그 신하가 상사병에 걸려 사경을 헤맨다는 소리니까.”
 34|
 35|“……!”
 36|
 37|경악한 호위장은 숨 쉬는 것조차 잊었다.
 38|
 39|미친놈이라는 것 정도는 짐작했지만, 아무리 그래도 천자를 향해 저런 불경한 말을 내뱉다니.
 40|
 41|황급히 주위의 인기척을 확인한 그는 간신히 목소리를 쥐어 짜냈다.
 42|
 43|“미, 미쳤습니까? 귀하가 누구인지는 모르지만 어찌 감히 황상 폐하께……!”
 44|
 45|“왜, 겁이라도 나느냐?”
 46|
 47|“그걸 말이라고 하십니까? 세상에, 다른 누군가가 들었다면 당장 반역죄로 몰렸을 겁니다.”
 48|
 49|“흠, 반역죄라.”
 50|
 51|잠시 생각하던 적천강이 턱을 긁적였다.
 52|
 53|예전 같았으면 모를까, 지금은 엄연히 제자를 둔 스승이자 무림맹에 속한 몸이었다.
 54|
 55|“그건 좀 곤란해질 수도 있겠군.”
 56|
 57|“곤란하다니. 무슨 반역죄가 무슨 경범죄인 줄 아시는 겁니까?”
 58|
 59|“그렇다고 구족(九族)을 멸할 만큼 큰 죄는 아니지. 천자도 결국 피륙으로 이루어진 사람일진대, 욕 좀 얻어먹는다 한들 무엇이 대수란 말이냐.”
 60|
 61|“……!”
 62|
 63|“네놈 얼굴이 참 볼만하구나. 크흐흐.”
 64|
 65|입만 딱 벌린 채 굳어 버린 호위장의 모습에, 적천강은 무릎을 치며 웃었다.
 66|
 67|이미 일백하고도 수십여 년을 살아온 그다.
 68|
 69|핏물이 마르지 않던 군웅할거(群雄割據)의 시대도, 새로운 통일 왕조의 탄생도 두 눈으로 직접 지켜보았다.
 70|
 71|천자에 대한 환상? 경외?
 72|
 73|웃기는 소리.
 74|
 75|아주 오랜 과거부터, 적천강에게 있어 천자라는 호칭이 가지는 의미는 그리 각별하지 않았다.
 76|
 77|‘그저 남들보다 조금 더 비범하며, 훨씬 더 큰 야망과 잔혹함을 지닌 자.’
 78|
 79|그것이 바로 적천강의 평가였고, 하나뿐인 제자의 말을 들은 후에는 더더욱 확신할 수 있었다.
 80|
 81|자신의 평가가 정확했다는 것을.
 82|
 83|천자는 하늘이 내리는 것이 아니라, 무수한 피와 시체 속에서 태어난다는 것을.
 84|
 85|적천강은 문득 진태경에게 들었던 이야기를 떠올렸다. 거대한 강철의 새를 하늘에 띄우고, 무수한 별들 사이를 누빈다는 그 놀라운 이야기들을.
 86|
 87|그런 생각과 함께 얼어붙어 있는 호위장의 모습을 보니, 다시 한번 터져 나오는 실소를 참을 수 없었다.
 88|
 89|“이해한다. 노부의 식견으로도 알지 못한 것이 산더미거늘, 네놈 같은 핏덩이가 어찌 짐작이나 할 수 있겠느냐.”
 90|
 91|“노, 노부? 핏덩이?”
 92|
 93|“세상은 넓고, 세월은 계속해서 흐른다. 아마도 삼천갑자 동방삭이라면 그 변화를 지켜볼 수 있겠지.”
 94|
 95|호위장은 넋이 나간 얼굴로 적천강을 바라보았다.
 96|
 97|기껏해야 동년배로 보이는 자가 구사하는 어휘가 너무 이질적인 탓도 있었지만, 그로서는 무엇 하나 이해할 수 없는 이야기들이기 때문이었다.
 98|
 99|“그게 도대체 무슨 소리…….”
100|
101|호위장이 말꼬리를 흐린 그때.
102|
103|“굳이 이해하려 하실 필요는 없습니다. 저런 이야기를 듣는다면 누구나 같은 의문을 품을 테니까요.”
104|
105|“……!”
106|
107|불현듯 귓가를 파고든 누군가의 목소리에, 헛숨을 삼킨 호위장은 본능적으로 허리춤에 찬 검을 뽑아 휘둘렀다.
108|
109|아니, 그러려고 했다.
110|
111|어디선가 터져 나온 끔찍하리만치 거대한 기운이, 그의 전신을 짓누르기 전까지는.
112|
113|화아악!
114|
115|불길처럼 뜨겁고, 만근거석처럼 무거운 기파(氣波).
116|
117|호위장은 감히 숨도 쉬지 못한 채 굳어 버렸다.
118|
119|어느덧 머리 위를 짓누르는 기운을 이기지 못하고 푹 꺾여 버린 고개.
120|
121|격동으로 파르르 떨리는 그의 시선은, 검 자루에 닿지도 못한 자신의 손을 향하고 있었다.
122|
123|‘어, 어떻게?’
124|
125|새하얗게 물든 호위장의 머릿속에서는 해결하지 못한 그 의문만이 둥둥 떠다녔다.
126|
127|어찌 이럴 수 있단 말인가.
128|
129|안락한 삶을 위해 무림을 떠나 관에 투신했어도 그는 절정 고수다.
130|
131|그것도 명문대파의 그늘에서 자란 온실 속 화초가 아닌, 실전이라면 이골이 난 낭인(浪人) 출신의 절정 고수.
132|
133|낭인으로 지낸 세월만 이십여 년이다.
134|
135|솜털이 나기 시작할 때쯤 전장에 뛰어들었고, 끈질긴 잡초가 되어 살아남았다.
136|
137|명문의 제자들처럼 훌륭한 무공을 익히지는 못했으나 사선(死線)을 넘나들며 쌓아 올린 경험은 그 이상이라고 자부했다.
138|
139|그런데…….
140|
141|‘움직이면, 죽는다.’
142|
143|선명하게 보인다. 또렷하게 느껴진다.
144|
145|성큼 다가온 죽음의 그림자가, 몇 번을 다시 태어난다 하더라도 결코 넘을 수 없을 거대한 벽이.
146|
147|툭.
148|
149|어느샌가 맺힌 식은땀 한 방울이, 호위장의 턱 끝을 타고 떨어져 내린 그 순간이었다.
150|
151|“날도 더운데, 손님을 상대로 장난이 과하십니다.”
152|
153|스아아.
154|
155|문득 들려온 평온한 목소리에 언제 그랬냐는 듯 흩어지는 열기.
156|
157|참았던 숨을 토해 내며 거칠게 심호흡하는 호위장의 귓가에, 두런두런 나누는 대화 소리가 전해졌다.
158|
159|“손님은 무슨. 부탁 같지도 않은 부탁을 하러 온 어중이떠중이일 뿐이다.”
160|
161|“정확히는 제 손님이지요. 애당초 저를 찾아오셨으니.”
162|
163|“세상천지에 어떤 손님이 다짜고짜 검부터 뽑으려 든단 말이냐?”
164|
165|“이해합니다. 넋이 나가 있는 상황에서 갑작스럽게 놀라면 그럴 수도 있는 것 아니겠습니까.”
166|
167|“시끄럽다. 네놈은 노부 덕분에 무사한 줄이나 알아라.”
168|
169|“감히 적 대협께 비할 수는 없겠으나, 저 역시 스승께 배운 한 수가 있으니 걱정하지 않으셔도 됩니다.”
170|
171|“아니, 그런데 이 머리에 피도 안 마른 놈이 아까부터 따박따박 말대꾸를……!”
172|
173|“의원으로서 견해를 말씀드리자면, 머리가 피가 마르면 죽습니다.”
174|
175|“마!”
176|
177|대화를 듣던 호위장은 혼란스러움을 느끼며 고개를 들었다.
178|
179|머리에 피도 안 마르긴커녕, 새하얀 백발을 늘어트린 노인이 인자한 눈빛으로 그를 바라보고 있었다.
180|
181|“괜찮으십니까?”
182|
183|“……!”
184|
185|그 순간. 호위장은 본능적으로 노인의 정체를 알아차렸다.
186|
187|흡사 신선과도 같은 풍모. 거기에 더해 앞서 들었던 대화 속에 모든 답이 있었다.
188|
189|“시, 신의(神醫)?”
190|
191|노인, 신의가 쓰게 웃으며 고개를 끄덕였다.
192|
193|“예, 맞습니다. 이 늙은이가 늦는 바람에 의도치 않게 결례를 범했군요.”
194|
195|“아, 아닙니다! 결례라니, 당치 않습니다!”
196|
197|호위장은 황급히 손을 내저으며 적천강의 눈치를 살폈다.
198|
199|마침내 신의와 마주하게 된 것은 기쁜 일이었지만, 저 무시무시한 대머리 중년인의 정체에 비하면 아무것도 아니었다.
200|
201|‘서, 설마.’
202|
203|흐트러졌던 머릿속 조각들이 순식간에 짜 맞춰지는 듯한 기분이었다.
204|
205|어림잡아도 칠순이 넘어 보이는 신의를 어린아이 취급하는 모습. 단순히 발산한 것만으로도 전신을 옥죄던 압도적인 기파.
206|
207|아니, 정확히는 열양지기.
208|
209|거기에 더해 마지막으로 조금 전 들었던 신의의 말까지.
210|
211|‘적 대협이라고 했다. 분명히.’
212|
213|호위장은 자신도 모르게 마른 침을 꿀꺽 삼켰다.
214|
215|헛소리다. 미친 생각이다.
216|
217|그러나 어쩔 수 없었다. 호위장이 알기로 이 모든 조건을 충족시킬 수 있는 사람은, 천하를 뒤집어 탈탈 털어도 한 사람뿐이었으니까.
218|
219|“저, 저분은 혹시 화, 화, 화…….”
220|
221|차마 말을 잇지 못하고 더듬거리는 호위장을 향해, 적천강이 눈살을 찌푸렸다.
222|
223|“그래, 노부가 바로 화왕(火王)이니라. 화화화왕이 아니라.”
224|
225|“히이익!”
226|
227|“……이놈 반응이 왠지 기분 나쁜데. 저승사자라도 된 기분이군.”
228|
229|도무지 이해할 수 없다는 듯한 적천강의 모습에, 신의는 문득 과거 스승에게 들었던 이야기를 떠올렸다.
230|
231|
232|
233|‘무림인이란 족속들은 기본적으로 멀리하는 것이 상책이다.’
234|
235|‘어째서입니까?’
236|
237|‘세상에 존재하는 모든 인간군상 중에서 가장 비열하고, 난폭하며, 심지어 멍청하기까지 하니까.’
238|
239|‘아, 어느 정도는 맞는 말 같군요.’
240|
241|‘……무슨 뜻이냐?’
242|
243|‘아무것도 아닙니다. 한데 제자는 모든 무림인이 그런 것은 아니라고 알고 있습니다만.’
244|
245|‘사실이지. 하지만 사마외도(邪魔外道)만큼은 믿고 걸러야 한다. 백중 구십구가 병신이니.’
246|
247|‘정파에는 뜻 있는 협객들이 있다고 들었습니다. 그들도 피해야 합니까?’
248|
249|‘어지간하면 피해라. 입으로만 인의(人義)를 논할 뿐, 그중 절반은 병신이다.’
250|
251|‘그렇다면 정파에도, 사마외도에도 속하지 않은 정사지간(正邪之間)의 무림인은 어떻습니까?’
252|
253|‘그들은 워낙 제멋대로인 데다 알려지지 않은 이들이 많기에 판단하기 어렵다. 그러나 이 스승의 경험에 따르면, 넌 두 개만 기억하면 된다.’
254|
255|‘그게 무엇입니까?’
256|
257|‘화왕. 열화문. 따라 하며 머릿속에 새기거라.’
258|
259|‘화왕. 열화문.’
260|
261|‘한 번으로는 부족하다. 이번에는 마음에 새기며 말해라.’
262|
263|‘화왕. 열화문.’
264|
265|‘잘했다. 이 두 개만 기억하거라.’
266|
267|‘화왕이라는 별호는 언뜻 들어본 것 같습니다만, 제자가 굳이 이렇게까지 기억해야 하는 이유가 무엇입니까?’
268|
269|‘피해라.’
270|
271|‘예?’
272|
273|‘그 어떤 상황에서도 절대 마주치지 마라. 만약 내가 없을 때 어디선가 화왕이 나타났다는 소문이 들리면, 아예 그 성(省)을 떠야 한다.’
274|
275|‘아니 무슨, 도대체 어떤 사람이기에 그렇게까지 해야 합니까?’
276|
277|‘미친놈이다.’
278|

[P71]
At the calm voice, the heat scattered as though it had never been there.

[P72]
The captain let out his held breath and began breathing hard. Voices reached his ears.

[P73]
“A guest? He’s some nobody here to make a request hardly worth calling one.”

[P74]
“He’s my guest, to be precise. He came to see me.”

[P75]
“What kind of guest tries to draw a sword the moment he arrives?”

[P76]
“I can understand it. He was already shaken, and then someone startled him.”

[P77]
“Quiet. You’re only safe thanks to this old man.”

[P78]
“I wouldn’t dare compare myself to you, Sir Jeok, but my Master did teach me a thing or two. You needn’t worry.”

[P79]
“Why, you little brat! You’ve been talking back to me this whole time, and the blood on your head isn’t even dry—”

[P80]
“As a physician, I should point out that if the blood in your head dries up, you die.”

[P81]
“Hey!”

[P82]
The captain lifted his head in confusion.

[P83]
The man Jeok Cheongang had called a wet-behind-the-ears brat had snow-white hair. He looked at the captain with kind eyes.

[P84]
“Are you all right?”

[P85]
“……!”

[P86]
The captain knew who he was at once.

[P87]
The old man had the bearing of an immortal, and their conversation had supplied the rest.

[P88]
“D-Divine Physician?”

[P89]
The old man—the Divine Physician—smiled wryly and nodded.

[P90]
“Yes. I arrived late and caused you trouble without meaning to.”

[P91]
“N-no! Not at all!”

[P92]
The captain waved his hands, then glanced nervously at Jeok Cheongang.

[P93]
Meeting the Divine Physician at last was wonderful. But it was nothing beside the question of who that terrifying bald, middle-aged man might be.

[P94]
*Could it be…?*

[P95]
The scattered pieces in his mind fell into place.

[P96]
Jeok treated the Divine Physician, who looked well past seventy, like a child. Merely releasing his qi had been enough to bind the captain’s entire body.

[P97]
No—more precisely, it was Scorching Yang Qi.

[P98]
And then there was what the Divine Physician had called him.

[P99]
*He said “Sir Jeok.” I heard him.*

[P100]
The captain swallowed.

[P101]
It was absurd. A crazy thought.

[P102]
But as far as he knew, only one person in the world fit every detail.

[P103]
“Th-that man… Could he be F-F-Fire—”

[P104]
Jeok Cheongang frowned at the stammering captain.

[P105]
“That’s right. I’m the Fire King. Not the F-F-Fire King.”

[P106]
“Eek!”

[P107]
“…Why does that reaction rub me the wrong way? You’d think I was the Grim Reaper.”

[P108]
At Jeok Cheongang’s baffled look, the Divine Physician remembered something his Master had once told him.

[P109]
> “As a rule, it’s best to keep your distance from martial artists.”
>
> “Why?”
>
> “Of all the kinds of people in the world, they’re the most vile, violent, and stupid.”
>
> “Ah, I suppose that’s true to some extent.”
>
> “…What do you mean by that?”
>
> “Nothing. But I thought not all martial artists were like that.”
>
> “True. But steer clear of those who follow demonic, heterodox arts. Ninety-nine out of a hundred are idiots.”
>
> “I’ve heard there are righteous heroes among the orthodox faction. Should I avoid them, too?”
>
> “If you can. They talk about benevolence and righteousness, but half of them are idiots.”
>
> “Then what about martial artists who belong to neither side?”
>
> “They do as they please, and little is known about many of them. They’re hard to judge. But in my experience, you only need to remember two things.”
>
> “What are they?”
>
> “The Fire King. The Fire Gate Clan. Repeat them and burn them into your mind.”
>
> “The Fire King. The Fire Gate Clan.”
>
> “Once isn’t enough. This time, say them and engrave them on your heart.”
>
> “The Fire King. The Fire Gate Clan.”
>
> “Good. Remember those two.”
>
> “I think I’ve heard the title Fire King before, but why must I remember it so well?”
>
> “Avoid him.”
>
> “Pardon?”
>
> “Never meet him, no matter what. If you hear he’s appeared somewhere while I’m away, leave the province altogether.”
>
> “What kind of person is he that I’d have to go that far?”
>
> “A madman.”
>
> “…?”
>
> “The Fire King—or rather, the Fire Gate Clan—are madmen who’ve spent generations fighting orthodox and heterodox martial artists alike. They beat people when they’re in a bad mood, when they’re in a good mood, and some days when they’re in neither.”
>
> “…How can people like that exist?”
>
> “They do. For more than three hundred years, that mad sect has bred—no, produced—one generation of insanely strong madmen after another.”

[P110]
The Divine Physician remembered that day clearly. His Master, renowned as the greatest assassin of all time and unfailingly composed, had used the word *mad* three times to impress the danger upon him.

[P111]
*Then why does Sir Jeok look so offended? It all sounds right to me.*

[P112]
He kept that thought to himself. Stopping Jeok Cheongang, who had seized the captain by the collar and begun shouting at him, came first.

[P113]
“Do I look that vicious to you? Huh?”

[P114]
“Eek! N-no!”

[P115]
“Then why is your voice shaking? Are you mocking me for being bald?”

[P116]
“Eek! I-I’m not! Please spare me!”

[P117]
“If your voice shakes one more time, I’ll strip every last hair off your body…!”

[P118]
“Sir Jeok, please. Calm down.”

[P119]
The Divine Physician sighed as he stopped Jeok, then turned to the trembling captain.

[P120]
“I happened to hear the gist of the situation. To get straight to the point, I can’t leave.”

[P121]
“W-what? Why not?”

[P122]
“From what you’ve told me, the City Lord is suffering from an unusual case of lovesickness. As a physician, I must tend to those who are sicker and in greater pain.”

[P123]
“B-but he’s behaving nothing like himself!”

[P124]
“That’s only natural. The person he loves has been taken from him. Imagine how he must feel. If the patients in my care improve, I’ll pay him a visit then…”

[P125]
The Divine Physician trailed off and looked toward the slightly open door.

[P126]
Hurried footsteps and ragged breathing drew closer, loud enough for everyone to hear. With them came the distinctive clank of armor, a sound seldom heard from a martial artist.

[P127]
Tap-tap-tap! Clank!

[P128]
Sure enough, a figure in gleaming armor soon ran up and stopped at the door, nearly collapsing.

[P129]
“You…”

[P130]
The captain’s eyes widened. He recognized a subordinate who should have remained at the City Lord’s residence.

[P131]
The man dragged in a ragged breath and cried out, “Th-the City Lord…!”

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). ## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

His head bowed under the weight. Trembling, he stared at his hand. It hadn’t even reached the hilt.

[P56]
*H-how?*

[P57]
The unanswered question was all that remained in his mind, blank with shock.

[P58]
How could this be?

[P59]
He’d left Murim for a comfortable life in government service, but he was still a Peak master.

[P60]
Nor was he some hothouse flower raised in the shelter of a prestigious sect. He’d come up as a wandering martial artist, a Peak master hardened by real combat.

[P61]
He’d spent more than twenty years as a wanderer. He’d gone to war when he was barely old enough to grow peach fuzz and survived like a stubborn weed.

[P62]
He might not have learned the fine martial arts taught to the disciples of great sects, but he was proud that his experience on the brink of death more than made up for it.

[P63]
And yet…

[P64]
*If I move, I die.*

[P65]
He could see it clearly. Feel it.

[P66]
Death’s shadow had drawn close. Before him stood a wall he could never overcome, no matter how many times he was reborn.

[P67]
Drip.

[P68]
A bead of cold sweat slipped from his chin.

[P69]
“It’s a hot day. That’s a bit much to put a guest through.”

[P70]
Ssshhh.

[P71]
At the calm voice, the heat scattered as though it had never been there.

[P72]
The captain let out his held breath and began breathing hard. Voices reached his ears.

[P73]
“A guest? He’s some nobody here to make a request hardly worth calling one.”

[P74]
“He’s my guest, to be precise. He came to see me.”

[P75]
“What kind of guest tries to draw a sword the moment he arrives?”

[P76]
“I can understand it. He was already shaken, and then someone startled him.”

[P77]
“Quiet. You’re only safe thanks to this old man.”

[P78]
“I wouldn’t dare compare myself to you, Sir Jeok, but my Master did teach me a thing or two. You needn’t worry.”

[P79]
“Why, you little brat! You’ve been talking back to me this whole time, and the blood on your head isn’t even dry—”

[P80]
“As a physician, I should point out that if the blood in your head dries up, you die.”

[P81]
“Hey!”

[P82]
The captain lifted his head in confusion.

[P83]
The man Jeok Cheongang had called a wet-behind-the-ears brat had snow-white hair. He looked at the captain with kind eyes.

[P84]
“Are you all right?”

[P85]
“……!”

[P86]
The captain knew who he was at once.

[P87]
The old man had the bearing of an immortal, and their conversation had supplied the rest.

[P88]
“D-Divine Physician?”

[P89]
The old man—the Divine Physician—smiled wryly and nodded.

[P90]
“Yes. I arrived late and caused you trouble without meaning to.”

[P91]
“N-no! Not at all!”

[P92]
The captain waved his hands, then glanced nervously at Jeok Cheongang.

[P93]
Meeting the Divine Physician at last was wonderful. But it was nothing beside the question of who that terrifying bald, middle-aged man might be.

[P94]
*Could it be…?*

[P95]
The scattered pieces in his mind fell into place.

[P96]
Jeok treated the Divine Physician, who looked well past seventy, like a child. Merely releasing his qi had been enough to bind the captain’s entire body.

[P97]
No—more precisely, it was Scorching Yang Qi.

[P98]
And then there was what the Divine Physician had called him.

[P99]
*He said “Sir Jeok.” I heard him.*

[P100]
The captain swallowed.

[P101]
It was absurd. A crazy thought.

[P102]
But as far as he knew, only one person in the world fit every detail.

[P103]
“Th-that man… Could he be F-F-Fire—”

[P104]
Jeok Cheongang frowned at the stammering captain.

[P105]
“That’s right. I’m the Fire King. Not the F-F-Fire King.”

[P106]
“Eek!”

[P107]
“…Why does that reaction rub me the wrong way? You’d think I was the Grim Reaper.”

[P108]
At Jeok Cheongang’s baffled look, the Divine Physician remembered something his Master had once told him.

[P109]
> “As a rule, it’s best to keep your distance from martial artists.”
>
> “Why?”
>
> “Of all the kinds of people in the world, they’re the most vile, violent, and stupid.”
>
> “Ah, I suppose that’s true to some extent.”
>
> “…What do you mean by that?”
>
> “Nothing. But I thought not all martial artists were like that.”
>
> “True. But steer clear of those who follow demonic, heterodox arts. Ninety-nine out of a hundred are idiots.”
>
> “I’ve heard there are righteous heroes among the orthodox faction. Should I avoid them, too?”
>
> “If you can. They talk about benevolence and righteousness, but half of them are idiots.”
>
> “Then what about martial artists who belong to neither side?”
>
> “They do as they please, and little is known about many of them. They’re hard to judge. But in my experience, you only need to remember two things.”
>
> “What are they?”
>
> “The Fire King. The Fire Gate Clan. Repeat them and burn them into your mind.”
>
> “The Fire King. The Fire Gate Clan.”
>
> “Once isn’t enough. This time, say them and engrave them on your heart.”
>
> “The Fire King. The Fire Gate Clan.”
>
> “Good. Remember those two.”
>
> “I think I’ve heard the title Fire King before, but why must I remember it so well?”
>
> “Avoid him.”
>
> “Pardon?”
>
> “Never meet him, no matter what. If you hear he’s appeared somewhere while I’m away, leave the province altogether.”
>
> “What kind of person is he that I’d have to go that far?”
>
> “A madman.”
>
> “…?”
>
> “The Fire King—or rather, the Fire Gate Clan—are madmen who’ve spent generations fighting orthodox and heterodox martial artists alike. They beat people when they’re in a bad mood, when they’re in a good mood, and some days when they’re in neither.”
>
> “…How can people like that exist?”
>
> “They do. For more than three hundred years, that mad sect has bred—no, produced—one generation of insanely strong madmen after another.”

[P110]
The Divine Physician remembered that day clearly. His Master, renowned as the greatest assassin of all time and unfailingly composed, had used the word *mad* three times to impress the danger upon him.

[P111]
*Then why does Sir Jeok look so offended? It all sounds right to me.*

[P112]
He kept that thought to himself. Stopping Jeok Cheongang, who had seized the captain by the collar and begun shouting at him, came first.

[P113]
“Do I look that vicious to you? Huh?”

[P114]
“Eek! N-no!”

[P115]
“Then why is your voice shaking? Are you mocking me for being bald?”

[P116]
“Eek! I-I’m not! Please spare me!”

[P117]
“If your voice shakes one more time, I’ll strip every last hair off your body…!”

[P118]
“Sir Jeok, please. Calm down.”

[P119]
The Divine Physician sighed as he stopped Jeok, then turned to the trembling captain.

[P120]
“I happened to hear the gist of the situation. To get straight to the point, I can’t leave.”

[P121]
“W-what? Why not?”

[P122]
“From what you’ve told me, the City Lord is suffering from an unusual case of lovesickness. As a physician, I must tend to those who are sicker and in greater pain.”

[P123]
“B-but he’s behaving nothing like himself!”

[P124]
“That’s only natural. The person he loves has been taken from him. Imagine how he must feel. If the patients in my care improve, I’ll pay him a visit then…”

[P125]
The Divine Physician trailed off and looked toward the slightly open door.

[P126]
Hurried footsteps and ragged breathing drew closer, loud enough for everyone to hear. With them came the distinctive clank of armor, a sound seldom heard from a martial artist.

[P127]
Tap-tap-tap! Clank!

[P128]
Sure enough, a figure in gleaming armor soon ran up and stopped at the door, nearly collapsing.

[P129]
“You…”

[P130]
The captain’s eyes widened. He recognized a subordinate who should have remained at the City Lord’s residence.

[P131]
The man dragged in a ragged breath and cried out, “Th-the City Lord…!”

[P132]

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
